audit.title: CCIP Billing
audit.summary: This page is a well-structured, formula-driven explanation of the CCIP billing model with a concrete network-fee table (percentages and USD amounts by lane) — its strongest GEO asset. The two biggest opportunities are (1) missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no `dateModified` in the served `<head>`) and (2) no symptom/question-phrased headings for how developers actually query fees ("how do I estimate CCIP fees", "why is my CCIP fee so high"). Honest verdict: solid reference content that under-indexes on discoverability and agent-parsability relative to its quality.

recommendations.title: Add machine-readable metadata (JSON-LD + canonical + dates)
recommendations.issue: measured facts: "JSON-LD: 0 block(s) … canonical: MISSING … dateModified absent"
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-05-19`, `about: "Chainlink CCIP billing"`, and a self-referential `<link rel="canonical">`; surface the last-updated date in a machine-visible field, not just body text.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and visible freshness raise parse-trust and citation rate; canonical prevents `.md`/HTML duplicate dilution.

recommendations.title: Add question/symptom-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.where: new H2 near the end, plus rephrase existing anchors
recommendations.issue: no headings match "how do I estimate CCIP fees" / "why is my CCIP fee so high"
recommendations.change: Add H2 "How do I estimate a CCIP fee?" (lead with: call `getFee` on the router) and a FAQ covering "Is unspent gas refunded?" (No), "Which tokens can pay fees?" (LINK + gas tokens/wrapped ERC-20), "Why does Solana add a fee?" (0.10 USD ATA generation).
recommendations.why: developers/agents query by symptom, not concept titles; question-phrased sections win retrieval that formula prose loses.

recommendations.title: State the canonical fee fact in the first liftable sentence
recommendations.issue: "The CCIP billing model uses the `feeToken` specified in the message…"
recommendations.change: Precede with a self-contained sentence: "CCIP charges a single fee on the source blockchain, calculated as blockchain fee + network fee, and payable in LINK or a supported gas token (or its wrapped ERC-20)."
recommendations.why: gives engines one verbatim-liftable canonical claim; resists parametric priors about per-hop or destination-side billing.

recommendations.title: Fix broken/typo markup
recommendations.where: "Determine Token Handling Mechanism" note and the `gas usage` formula
recommendations.issue: `(/ccip/directory/testnet)` is not a link; trailing backtick in `gas for token transfers``
recommendations.change: Make it `[testnet](/ccip/directory/testnet)`; remove the stray backtick.
recommendations.why: malformed links break internal-graph traversal; formula typos degrade agent extraction.

recommendations.title: Tag the formula fences and add one worked example
recommendations.issue: measured facts: "5 untagged … languages: [none]"; no numeric worked example
recommendations.change: Tag blocks (e.g. ```text``` or ```` ```solidity ```` where applicable) and add one end-to-end example computing a fee for a named lane using table values.
recommendations.why: labeled blocks and a concrete calculation are highly liftable and quotable.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with numbers or drop them
recommendations.issue: "significantly reduce friction", "quickly scale CCIP to more blockchains"
recommendations.change: Cut the marketing framing or replace with a concrete fact (e.g., number of supported fee tokens/chains).
recommendations.why: quantitative claims outrank qualitative prose; fluff is neutral-to-negative.

antiPatterns: Marketing-flavored qualifiers ("significantly reduce friction", "quickly scale") in the intro.
Untagged code/formula fences (5 of 5, per measured facts).
One broken link (`/ccip/directory/testnet`) and one stray backtick in a formula.
No stale-content risk in body (dated 2025-05-19), but the date is not machine-exposed.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good; confirm this page is indexed there under a billing/fee entry.
Site-level: absence of JSON-LD and canonical appears template-wide; a shared docs-layout fix would lift many pages at once.
Freshness cadence: the fee table is time-sensitive (USD/percentage values) — ensure `dateModified` updates whenever the table changes so engines don't cite stale figures.
